q.s: In the Harappan civilisation, a 'sealing' refers to:
o: The clay impression of a seal pressed on a package
A stone weight used in trade
A copper coin of fixed value
q.x: A sealing is the clay impression of a seal pressed on the knot of a package; an intact sealing showed the goods were untouched.

q.s: Harappan seals were mainly used for:
q.x: Seals were used to stamp and mark goods in trade; they were not coins.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, the centre of Aryan culture shifted to:
q.x: In the Later Vedic period the core shifted east from the Punjab to the Ganga–Yamuna Doab.

q.s: Buddhism split into Mahayana and Hinayana after which Buddhist Council?
q.x: At the Fourth Council (Kanishka's time) differences over Bodhisattva and image worship led to the Mahayana–Hinayana split.

q.s: In Jainism, 'Sallekhana' means:
q.x: Sallekhana (Santhara) is the ritual fast unto death, as Chandragupta Maurya did at Shravanabelagola. Samvatsari is the forgiveness day.

q.s: Samvatsari, the Jain day of forgiveness, falls at the end of:
q.x: Samvatsari, the forgiveness day, is the last day of Paryushana.

q.s: The Sudarshana lake at Girnar was originally built by Pushyagupta, governor of:
q.x: Pushyagupta, Chandragupta Maurya's governor, built it; Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka; Rudradaman I and Skandagupta repaired it.

q.s: Which of the following rulers is NOT associated with building or repairing the Sudarshana lake at Girnar?
q.x: Chandragupta Maurya's governor built it, Ashoka's governor added canals, and Rudradaman I and Skandagupta repaired it; Samudragupta has no link with it.

q.s: Which historian attributed the decline of the Mauryan Empire to Ashoka's pacifist policy?
q.x: Raychaudhuri blamed Ashoka's pacifism; Kosambi stressed financial crisis, Thapar over-centralisation, H.P. Shastri a Brahmanical reaction.

q.s: Which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka refers to the appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas?
q.x: RE V records the Dhamma Mahamattas; RE I bans animal sacrifice, RE III the five-yearly tours of officials, RE VIII Dhammayatras.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rock Edict III – Tours of rajukas and pradeshikas
q.x: Rock Edict I bans animal sacrifice and festive gatherings (samaja).

q.s: In Gupta inscriptions, 'Halivakara' was a tax on:
q.x: Halivakara was the plough tax paid by every cultivator owning a plough; Uparikara was probably on temporary tenants.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a revenue term of the Gupta period?
q.x: Zabti was the Mughal revenue system of Akbar's time.

q.s: The dynastic emblem of the Guptas was:
q.x: The Guptas, Vaishnavas styled Parama Bhagavata, used Garuda as their emblem.

q.s: The colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri was carved in the reign of:
q.x: The Udayagiri Varaha belongs to the reign of Chandragupta II.

q.s: Kulottunga I, who united the Chola and Eastern Chalukya lines, was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and:
q.x: Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I, married Rajaraja Narendra and was the mother of Kulottunga I.

q.s: Under the Cholas, 'Mummudicholamandalam' was the name given to:
q.x: Mummudicholamandalam was northern Sri Lanka; Jayankondacholamandalam was the former Pallava Tondaimandalam.

q.s: Zafar Khan, Alauddin Khalji's general, was killed fighting the Mongols in 1299 at:
q.x: Zafar Khan charged the Mongols under Qutlugh Khwaja at Kili without support and was cut off and killed.

q.s: Who among the following Lodi rulers had the longest reign?
q.x: Bahlol Lodi (1451-89), who conquered Jaunpur, had the longest Lodi reign.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a ruler of the Lodi dynasty?
q.x: Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty; Bahlol, his son Sikandar and Ibrahim were Lodis.

q.s: Khizr Khan, founder of the Sayyid dynasty, ruled as a deputy of:
q.x: Khizr Khan did not take the title of Sultan as he accepted the suzerainty of Timur's son Shah Rukh.

q.s: Which traveller recorded the practice of sati in the Sultanate period?
q.x: Ibn Battuta recorded sati in the 14th century; Al-Biruni came earlier, with Mahmud of Ghazni.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Purdah was unknown in the Sultanate period.
Purdah spread among upper-class women of north India from the 13th century.
Al-Biruni recorded sati in the Sultanate period.
The jauhar at Ranthambhor took place in 1303.
q.x: Purdah spread from the 13th century. Ranthambhor's jauhar was in 1301 (Chittor 1303); Ibn Battuta recorded sati.

q.s: The earliest Persian treatise on Indian music is:
q.x: Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise; Rag Vibodh is Somanatha's, Man Kautuhal is linked to Raja Man Singh Tomar.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a treatise on music?
q.x: Tuzuk-i-Babri is Babur's memoir; the others are works on music.

q.s: Which Mughal emperor was called 'Shah-i-Bekhabar'?
q.x: Bahadur Shah I, Aurangzeb's successor who released Shahu, was called Shah-i-Bekhabar.

q.s: Banda Bahadur was executed in 1716 during the reign of:
q.x: Banda Bahadur was executed in 1716 under Farrukhsiyar.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Sufi saint – title) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Garib Nawaz is Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer; Nizamuddin Auliya was called Mehboob-e-Ilahi.

q.s: Which Chishti saint was called 'Ganj-i-Shakar'?
q.x: Baba Farid was known as Ganj-i-Shakar.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT a saint of the Chishti order?
q.x: Bahauddin Zakariya of Multan belonged to the Suhrawardi order.

q.s: The Portuguese lost Salsette and Bassein in 1739 to:
q.x: The Marathas took Salsette and Bassein in 1739; Hormuz was lost in 1622, Nagapattinam (1658) and Cochin (1663) to the Dutch.

q.s: Which of the following places was NOT lost by the Portuguese to the Dutch?
q.x: Hormuz was lost in 1622 to the Persians with English help; the Dutch took Colombo, Nagapattinam and Cochin.

q.s: The 'Golden Farman' (1632) allowing the English to trade freely in Golconda's ports was issued by:
q.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah issued it; the English paid 500 pagodas a year.

q.s: Who was accepted by the rebels as the symbolic head of the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: Bahadur Shah II, the Mughal emperor, was the symbolic head of the revolt.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Nana Saheb was the symbolic head of the Revolt of 1857.
The Revolt of 1857 was guided by a clear idea of a nation-state.
The Royal Indian Navy revolt of 1946 began on HMIS Talwar.
The Revolt of 1857 began as a peasant rebellion.
q.x: The RIN revolt began on HMIS Talwar. The 1857 revolt began as a sepoy mutiny, had no clear nation-state idea, and Bahadur Shah II was its symbolic head.

q.s: Secunderabad is named after which Nizam?
q.x: The Secunderabad cantonment is named after Sikandar Jah.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Asaf Jah I – Battle of Shakar Kheda (1724)
q.x: The Berar Treaty was signed in Nasir-ud-Daula's reign; Secunderabad is named after Sikandar Jah.

q.s: The policy of 'Subordinate Isolation' towards the Indian states is associated with:
q.x: Lord Hastings (1813-23) followed subordinate isolation; ring-fence was Warren Hastings', Doctrine of Lapse Dalhousie's.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (policy – author) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Doctrine of Lapse was Dalhousie's; Wellesley is known for the Subsidiary Alliance.

q.s: During 1857, the attack on the Hyderabad Residency was led by:
q.x: On 17 July 1857 Turrebaz Khan attacked the Residency to free Chida Khan; Col. Davidson repulsed it.

q.s: Who ended Clive's Dual Government in Bengal in 1772?
q.x: In 1772 Warren Hastings ended Dual Government and moved the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Warren Hastings raised the tribute to Shah Alam to Rs 26 lakh.
William Jones translated the Code of Gentoo Laws.
Warren Hastings moved the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta in 1772.
Warren Hastings set up the district adalats in 1793.
q.x: Hastings moved the treasury in 1772. The adalats date from 1772 (1793 is the Cornwallis Code); Halhed translated the Code; Hastings stopped the tribute.

q.s: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 occurred during the tenure of:
q.x: Barlow (1805-07) saw the Vellore Mutiny; Minto I signed the Treaty of Amritsar (1809).

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lord Minto I – Treaty of Amritsar
Sir John Shore – Treaty of Amritsar
q.x: Sir John Shore followed non-intervention; the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) was concluded under Minto I.

q.s: The Act that exempted the Governor-General-in-Council from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction for official acts was:
q.x: The Amending (Act of Settlement) Act of 1781 also excluded revenue matters from the Court.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Amending Act, 1781?
o: Respect for the customs of Indians
Exclusion of revenue matters from the Supreme Court
Exemption of the Governor-General-in-Council for official acts
Creation of the Board of Control
q.x: The Board of Control came with Pitt's India Act, 1784.

q.s: The Chalisa famine of North India occurred in:
q.x: Chalisa – 1783-84; Great Bengal Famine – 1770; Doji Bara – 1791-92; Orissa famine – 1865-66.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Chalisa famine was in 1783-84.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT an Orientalist in the Orientalist–Anglicist debate?
q.x: Trevelyan, like Macaulay and James Mill, was an Anglicist.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Orientalists rejected all Western subjects.
Charles Trevelyan was a leading Orientalist.
In Madras, Thomas Munro backed vernacular schooling.
q.x: Munro backed pathashalas. Mill and Trevelyan were Anglicists; Orientalists accepted some Western subjects.

q.s: The Lee Commission (1923-24) on the civil services was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Lee – Reading; Islington – Hardinge II; Aitchison – Dufferin; Statutory Civil Service – Lytton.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (commission – viceroy) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Islington Commission (1912-15) was appointed under Hardinge II.

q.s: The East India College that trained Company civil servants from 1806 was located at:
q.x: The East India College was at Haileybury; Addiscombe was the military seminary.

q.s: The College of Fort William (1800) was founded by:
q.x: Wellesley founded the College of Fort William in 1800 to train civil servants.

q.s: During the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909), John Morley was:
q.x: John Morley was Secretary of State; Minto II was Viceroy, succeeding Curzon in 1905.

q.s: India's first trade union, the Madras Labour Union (1918), was formed among the workers of:
q.x: The Madras Labour Union (April 1918) was formed among Buckingham and Carnatic Mills workers.

q.s: India's first May Day was celebrated at Madras in 1923 by:
q.x: Singaravelu Chettiar organised the first May Day in 1923.

q.s: Under the Indian Constitution, the 'Instrument of Instructions' of the 1935 Act was the model for:
q.x: The Instrument of Instructions became the Directive Principles.

q.s: Which provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 never came into operation?
q.x: Central dyarchy depended on the federation, which never came into being.

q.s: Who among the following was the first Andhra Brahmo and edited the 'Hindu Reformer'?
q.x: Mannava Butchaiah Pantulu, first Andhra Brahmo, edited the Hindu Reformer.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT one of the 'Brahmo Trinity' of Andhra?
q.x: The Brahmo Trinity was Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu and Peda Bapayya.

q.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Andhra Drama'?
q.x: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu is the Father of Andhra Drama; Andhra Ratna was Duggirala, Kavi Raju was Tripuraneni.

q.s: Who founded the Stree Samajam (1902), an early women's association in Andhra?
q.x: Bhandaru Acchamamba founded the Stree Samajam in 1902.

q.s: The Andhra Desa Library Association (1914) is associated with:
q.x: Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah is the pioneer of the library movement in Andhra.

q.s: Which party was founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1942?
q.x: Ambedkar founded the Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942 (the Independent Labour Party was 1936).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
q.x: The Swaraj Party was founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

q.s: Vande Mataram was adopted as India's National Song on:
q.x: The Constituent Assembly adopted it as the National Song on 24 January 1950.

q.s: Vande Mataram was first sung at an INC session in 1896 by:
q.x: Tagore sang it at the Calcutta session of 1896.

q.s: Ram Prasad Bismil, the Kakori conspiracy revolutionary, was hanged in December 1927 at:
q.x: Bismil – Gorakhpur; Ashfaqullah Khan – Faizabad; Roshan Singh – Naini; Rajendra Lahiri – Gonda.

q.s: Bhagat Singh was born in the year:
q.x: Bhagat Singh was born in 1907; Chandrashekhar Azad in 1906 and Khudiram Bose in 1889.

q.s: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Azad shot Saunders in 1928 to avenge the death of:
q.x: Lajpat Rai died of injuries from the lathi charge on the anti-Simon procession at Lahore; Saunders was shot in December 1928.

q.s: During the Quit India Movement, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, as a CWC member, was imprisoned at:
q.x: CWC members including Pattabhi were held at Ahmednagar Fort; Gandhi was at the Aga Khan Palace.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra in the Quit India Movement is correct?
o: Duvvuri Subbamma faced a lathi charge at Tenali.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed for the first time in 1942.
Pattabhi Sitaramayya was held at the Aga Khan Palace.
Chitturi Annapurna Devi was arrested at Guntur at the age of 17.
q.x: Annapurna Devi, 17, was arrested at Guntur. Subbamma's lathi charge was at Peddapuram; Unnava was jailed again; Pattabhi was at Ahmednagar Fort.

q.s: Under which Article of the Constitution can only Parliament prescribe residence requirements for public employment?
q.x: Art 16(3); hence in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao (1969) the Supreme Court struck down the Telangana residence clause of the 1957 Act.

q.s: Jwalapuram, an Upper Palaeolithic site, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Jwalapuram is in Kurnool district; Giddaluru, Dornala and Yerragondapalem are in Prakasam.

q.s: Which of the following Palaeolithic sites is NOT in Prakasam district?
q.x: Jwalapuram is in Kurnool district.

q.s: Who identified about 12 types of megalithic burials in Andhra?
q.x: N.R. Banerji classified about 12 types; iron implements and black-and-red ware were usual grave goods.

q.s: India's largest collection of anthropomorphic megalithic figures is found near:
q.x: Anthropomorphic figures – Tirupati; menhir – Revarala; ram-shaped sarcophagi – Sankhavaram and Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a type of megalithic burial?
q.x: A stupa is a Buddhist monument, not a megalithic burial.

q.s: Vengipuram, the ancient capital of the Eastern Chalukyas, is identified with:
q.x: Vengipuram is Pedavegi near Eluru.

q.s: In early Andhra, which dynasty was famed as road builders ('Mahapatha nirmatalu')?
q.x: The Satavahanas were the famed road builders, not the Ikshvakus.

q.s: Sriparvataswamy was the family deity of the:
q.x: Sriparvataswamy was the Vishnukundin family deity; they bore the titles Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya.

q.s: According to the Mahavamsa, who took Buddhism from the Pallava-bhoga region to Sri Lanka?
q.x: The Mahavamsa credits Mahadeva Bhikshu; Ceylonese monks also used Nagarjunakonda as a Hinayana base.

q.s: The Buddhist site of Salihundam in Srikakulam district was discovered by:
q.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy found Salihundam; Thotlakonda was spotted by the Indian Navy.

q.s: Which Buddhist site near Visakhapatnam was spotted by the Indian Navy during an aerial survey?
q.x: Thotlakonda was spotted by the Navy and is known for rainwater harvesting.

q.s: A 12th-century Bezawada inscription remembers which Vishnukundin ruler for sentencing his own son for killing a poor woman's son?
q.x: Madhava Varma II is remembered for justice: he sentenced his son to death.

q.s: The Rashtrakuta line was overthrown around 973 by:
q.x: Tailapa II of the Kalyani Chalukyas overthrew it after Paramara Siyaka II sacked Manyakheta in 972.

q.s: The temples of the Kalyani Chalukyas in the Gadag style were mainly built of:
q.x: Soft chloritic schist allowed fine carving; their star-shaped plans became a Hoysala model.

q.s: Errana, the third of the Kavitrayam, was patronised by:
q.x: Errana was court poet of the Reddi king Prolaya Vema; Tikkana served Manumasiddhi II.

q.s: Who among the following is NOT one of the Kavitrayam who translated the Mahabharata into Telugu?
q.x: The Kavitrayam are Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana; Pothana wrote the Telugu Bhagavatam.

q.s: The 'Shiva Kavi Yugam' of Telugu literature is dated:
q.x: The Shiva Kavi Yugam spans 1060-1260.

q.s: Jahaz Mahal and Hindola Mahal at Mandu were built by:
q.x: Ghiyasuddin Khalji built them; Hoshang Shah's tomb is India's first marble tomb.

q.s: India's first marble tomb is that of:
q.x: Hoshang Shah's tomb at Mandu is the first marble tomb in India.

q.s: In Vijayanagara, 'Kalyana Kanika' was a tax levied on:
q.x: Kalyana Kanika – wedding tax on both parties; Putrodaya Kanuka – birth of a son; Meruka – sale and purchase.

q.s: The founder of the Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara was:
q.x: Tirumala Raya, brother of Aliya Rama Raya, founded the fourth dynasty, named after Araviti in Kurnool.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara?
q.x: Vijayanagara's dynasties were Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu; the Bahmanis were its rivals.

q.s: The title 'Andhra Suratrana' was borne by:
q.x: Andhra Suratrana was Kapaya Nayaka's title; the Velamas took Jagadabbaganda and Rayavesa Bhujanga.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Singama was killed at Jallipalli by the Jallipalli Kshatriyas aided by the Reddis.
Singama was killed at Dharanikota by Anavota Reddi.
Anavota Reddi defeated Madanayudu and Naganayudu at Dharanikota.
After Dharanikota the Velamas took the title Andhra Suratrana.
q.x: Singama died at Jallipalli; at Dharanikota the Velamas defeated Anavota Reddi and took Jagadabbaganda and Rayavesa Bhujanga.

q.s: Which Recherla Velama ruler shifted the capital from Amanagallu to Rachakonda?
q.x: Anapota Nayaka moved the capital to Rachakonda; his brother Mada Nayaka ruled Devarakonda.

q.s: Which of the following foreign travellers did NOT describe sati in Vijayanagara?
q.x: Nuniz, Conti and Barbosa describe sati; Abdur Razzaq is not among them.

q.s: Who among the following was a learned woman of the Vijayanagara period?
q.x: Gangadevi (author of Madhuravijayam) and Tirumalamba were learned women of Vijayanagara.

q.s: In Vijayanagara society, 'Kanyashulkam' meant:
q.x: Kanyashulkam – bride price; Varashulkam – dowry; Benabaga – slavery.

q.s: In the Company period, the headquarters of the Krishna collectorate was:
q.x: The Krishna collectorate was headquartered at Machilipatnam.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the eight Andhra collectorates of 1856?
q.x: The eight were Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna, Nellore, Bellary, Cuddapah and Kurnool.

q.s: The Battle of Tallikota (1565) is also known as the Battle of:
q.x: Tallikota is also called Rakshasi-Tangadi.

q.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy was publicly hanged in 1847 near:
q.x: He was hanged near Koilakuntla on 22 February 1847; Uyyalawada was in Kurnool district, now Nandyal.

q.s: The Buckingham Canal, part of National Waterway-4, runs parallel to the:
q.x: It is a salt-water navigation canal along the Coromandel coast, extended as famine relief in 1876-78.

q.s: A National College was established in Andhra during the Non-Cooperation Movement at:
q.x: The National College was at Eluru (Machilipatnam's Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala is the other famous one); Pallepadu Ashram was in Nellore.

q.s: Which Telugu poet was called 'Abhinava Nannaya'?
q.x: Rayaprolu Subbarao – Abhinava Nannaya; Duvvuri Ramireddy – Kavi Kokila.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Telugu Lenka was Tummala Sitarama Murthy.

q.s: The Madras Public Libraries Bill of 1938 was drafted and moved by:
q.x: Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya moved it; the Madras Public Libraries Act came in 1948.

q.s: The first widow remarriage in Andhra was performed by Veeresalingam at Rajahmundry in:
q.x: The first widow remarriage was on 11 December 1881.

q.s: The first World Telugu Conference was held in:
q.x: The first World Telugu Conference was held at Hyderabad in 1975.

q.s: Mohiniattam is a classical dance of:
q.x: Mohiniattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (classical dance – State) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Mohiniattam belongs to Kerala.

q.s: The Chenchu tribe of Andhra Pradesh mainly lives in the:
q.x: Chenchus inhabit the Nallamala; Koya and Konda Reddi live in the Godavari region; Savara and Jatapu in Srikakulam-Vizianagaram.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (tribe – main region) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Yanadis live mainly in Nellore, Chittoor and Prakasam.

q.s: The Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly was moved on 13 December 1946 by:
q.x: Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946; it was adopted on 22 January 1947.

q.s: The first sitting of the Constituent Assembly was held on:
q.x: It first met on 9 December 1946; the Muslim League boycotted it.

q.s: Under Article 350-B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the:
q.x: Article 350-B: the President appoints the Special Officer.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Integration Council is correct?
o: It is chaired by the Home Minister.
It is chaired by the Prime Minister.
It is a statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament.
q.x: The NIC (1961), chaired by the PM, is non-statutory, set up by executive decision.

q.s: In Max Weber's typology, authority based on custom and the sanctity of tradition is called:
q.x: Traditional authority rests on custom; charismatic authority on the leader's personality.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Max Weber's types of authority?
q.x: Weber's three types are traditional, charismatic and legal-rational.

q.s: Among the Khasis of Meghalaya, property is inherited by the:
q.x: Khasis follow ultimogeniture: the youngest daughter inherits.

q.s: The Marumakkathayam system of matrilineal inheritance was followed by the:
q.x: Marumakkathayam was the Nair system, abolished by the Kerala Joint Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975.

q.s: The nodal agency for the National Family Health Survey is:
o: International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
q.x: IIPS, Mumbai is the nodal agency for NFHS.

q.s: According to Max Weber, the three dimensions of social stratification are:
q.x: Weber's three dimensions are class, status and party (power); caste is a closed status group.

q.s: Article 16(4A), providing reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, was inserted by the:
q.x: 77th – 16(4A); 81st – 16(4B) carry-forward; 82nd – proviso to Art 335; 85th – consequential seniority.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 82nd Amendment – Relaxed qualifying marks in promotion
q.x: The 85th Amendment gave consequential seniority; 16(4B) came with the 81st.

q.s: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 15 August 2020 by the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
q.x: MoSJE launched it, first in 272 districts; it is implemented through the National Institute of Social Defence.

q.s: The 'Kashi Declaration' (July 2025) is associated with:
o: Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat
q.x: The Kashi Declaration came out of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports' Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat summit.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an independent think tank?
q.x: CPR, NCAER, PRS and ORF are independent; the National Innovation Council (2010) was a Government think tank.

q.s: Which expert group on poverty dropped the calorie anchor and used the Mixed Reference Period?
q.x: Tendulkar (2009) dropped the calorie norm; Alagh used 2,400/2,100 calories; Lakdawala made State-specific lines.

q.s: The Rangarajan Expert Group on poverty submitted its report in:
q.x: Rangarajan (2014) returned to food plus non-food needs such as housing and transport.

q.s: Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: MKSP is a sub-component of DAY-NRLM under the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate offers interest of:
q.x: The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate runs 2 years at 7.5%.

q.s: Under PMMVY 2.0, the benefit for a second child is given only if:
o: The birth is in a government hospital
q.x: The ₹6,000 second-child benefit is given only for a girl, to discourage sex selection.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Regular government employees are eligible under PMMVY 2.0.
Before PMMVY 2.0, the ₹5,000 benefit covered the first two live births.
PMMVY has been implemented from 1 January 2017.
PMMVY 2.0 gives the second-child benefit whether the child is a boy or a girl.
q.x: The ₹5,000 was for the first child only; the second-child benefit is only for a girl; regular government employees are excluded.

q.s: Ujjawala, a scheme for prevention of trafficking and rescue of victims, is run by the:
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: Ujjawala is an MWCD scheme; Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (LPG) belongs to the Petroleum Ministry.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three umbrella missions of the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
q.x: Mission Indradhanush is the Health Ministry's immunisation mission.

q.s: The 'Har Khet Ko Pani' motto belongs to:
q.x: Har Khet Ko Pani / Per Drop More Crop is PMKSY; JJM aims at a tap connection for every rural household.

q.s: NIPUN Bharat aims at:
o: Foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 3
Free online courses for higher education
q.x: NIPUN Bharat (2021) targets FLN by Grade 3; SWAYAM offers MOOCs; PM-Vidyalaxmi gives education loans; Vidyanjali links volunteers.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (programme – objective) is NOT correctly matched?
o: NIPUN Bharat – Foundational literacy and numeracy
q.x: SWAYAM offers free online courses (MOOCs).

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the '104' service refers to:
q.x: 104 – mobile medical units with fixed-day village visits; 108 – emergency ambulance.

q.s: The Family Physician programme of Andhra Pradesh was launched on 6 April 2023 at:
q.x: It was launched at Lingamguntla in Chilakaluripet, Palnadu district.

q.s: In Sukanya Shantha v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court struck down caste-based work allocation in prisons as violating:
q.x: The Court held caste-based prison work violated Article 17, among others.

q.s: The National Human Rights Commission is constituted under the:
q.x: The NHRC was set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

q.s: Under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, which Section bars anticipatory bail?
q.x: s.18 bars anticipatory bail; s.14A – appeal within 90 days; s.15 – Special Public Prosecutors; s.19 – no probation.

q.s: Under the Instrument of Accession (1947), Jammu and Kashmir ceded to India:
o: All subjects of the Union List
q.x: Only defence, external affairs and communications were ceded.

q.s: India referred the Kashmir issue on 1 January 1948 to the:
q.x: India approached the UN Security Council under Article 35 of the UN Charter.

q.s: The Shangri-La Dialogue, where India set out its Indo-Pacific vision in 2018, is organised by:
q.x: The IISS organises the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: India set out its Indo-Pacific vision at the Shangri-La Dialogue in 2018.
The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative has five pillars.
The Shangri-La Dialogue is organised by Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The Shangri-La Dialogue is held at Jakarta.
q.x: PM Modi spoke at Shangri-La in June 2018. The Dialogue is organised by the IISS in Singapore; the IPOI has seven pillars.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the '4 Cs' of India's Act East Policy?
q.x: The 4 Cs are Commerce, Culture, Connectivity and Capacity building; the North-East is the gateway to ASEAN.

q.s: The US 'Pivot to Asia' (Rebalance) policy was announced under President:
q.x: It was announced under Obama in 2011.

q.s: India-US relations are officially described as a:
q.x: Since 2020, ties are a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership; the 2008 nuclear deal was the turning point.

q.s: The G20 accounts for about what share of world GDP?
q.x: The G20 has about 85% of world GDP and two-thirds of world population.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Expanded BRICS has about a quarter of the world's population.
The G20 accounts for about one-third of the world's population.
The G20 accounts for about 85% of world GDP.
In 2011 BRICS had about 20% of IMF votes but 11% of world GDP.
q.x: The G20 has 85% of world GDP and two-thirds of population; expanded BRICS has about half the population; in 2011 BRICS had 20% of GDP but 11% of IMF votes.

q.s: Pakistan was removed from the FATF grey list in:
q.x: Placed on the grey list in June 2018, Pakistan was removed in October 2022; it was never black-listed.

q.s: Under UNCLOS, the Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to:
q.x: EEZ – 200 nm; territorial sea – 12 nm; contiguous zone – 24 nm.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (maritime zone – extent) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Continental shelf – up to 350 nautical miles
q.x: The contiguous zone extends to 24 nautical miles.

q.s: The Malabar naval exercise began in 1992 as a bilateral exercise between India and:
q.x: Malabar began as India-US; Japan became permanent in 2015 and Australia rejoined in 2020.

q.s: The first AIKEYME naval exercise between India and African navies was held in 2025 in:
q.x: The first AIKEYME was hosted at Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

q.s: The Indian Independence Bill received royal assent on:
q.x: Introduced 4 July, royal assent 18 July 1947; the Radcliffe award came on 17 August.

q.s: The procedure for impeachment of the President in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
q.x: Impeachment of the President, judicial independence and the Vice-President's office come from the USA.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT borrowed from the Constitution of the USA?
q.x: The parliamentary system came from Britain.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (feature – source) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency – Weimar Germany
q.x: Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the USSR.

q.s: Article 370 was declared inoperative in August 2019 by a Presidential order under:
q.x: Article 370(3) allowed the President to declare it inoperative by public notification.

q.s: Article 329A was omitted from the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 39th inserted Art 329A; the 44th omitted it.

q.s: Part VII of the Constitution, dealing with Part B States, was repealed by the:
q.x: The 7th Amendment (1956) abolished the classification of States into Parts A, B, C and D.

q.s: The PIO card was merged with the OCI card by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act of:
q.x: 2015 merged PIO with OCI; 2003 introduced Overseas Citizenship; 2005 widened it.

q.s: Which State has been placed under President's Rule the most number of times?
q.x: Manipur (11) leads, followed by Uttar Pradesh (10).

q.s: Which of the following States has never been under President's Rule?
q.x: Chhattisgarh and Telangana have never had President's Rule.

q.s: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in:
q.x: The PoA Act was enacted in 1989; the PCR Act in 1955.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The PoA Act was enacted in 1955.
Under the PoA Act, if an innocent SC/ST person is executed due to false evidence, the punishment is death.
Under the PoA Act, such an execution is punished only with imprisonment for life.
Fabricating false evidence for a capital offence is punished with seven years' imprisonment.
q.x: Fabricating such evidence is punished with life imprisonment; if the innocent person is executed, with death. The Act is of 1989.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the President and Governors from being answerable to any court for official acts?
q.x: Article 361; Art 361A protects true reports of legislative proceedings; Art 105 protects MPs.

q.s: Article 21A (Right to Education) was inserted by the:
q.x: The 86th Amendment, 2002 inserted Article 21A.

q.s: Under Article 22, a person may be held in preventive detention without an Advisory Board's report for up to:
q.x: Detention beyond three months needs an Advisory Board report.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the right to life does not include the right to die, upholding Section 309 IPC?
q.x: Gian Kaur overruled P. Rathinam, which had struck down Section 309.

q.s: The 44th Amendment, 1978 shifted the right to property to Article 300A in Part:
q.x: It omitted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A in Part XII, making property a legal right.

q.s: The 44th Constitutional Amendment was passed under the government of:
q.x: The Janata government of Morarji Desai passed it.

q.s: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children in factories, mines and hazardous work below the age of:
q.x: Article 24 bars children below 14.

q.s: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is NOT available to foreigners?
q.x: Article 19 freedoms are for citizens only; Articles 14, 20 and 21 are available to all persons.

q.s: In the Constitution, 'SEBC' stands for:
q.x: SEBC means Socially and Educationally Backward Classes; 'Backward Classes' itself is not defined.

q.s: India's first National Policy for Children was adopted in:
q.x: The first was in 1974; the 2013 policy defines a child as below 18.

q.s: Under the National Policy for Children, 2013, a child is a person below:
q.x: The 2013 policy defines a child as a person below 18.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise the right to free education up to 14 years as part of Article 21?
o: Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
q.x: Unni Krishnan (1993) limited the right under Art 21 to free education up to 14 years.

q.s: Presidential assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill was made obligatory by the:
q.x: The 24th Amendment made assent obligatory.

q.s: Which of the following statements about a Constitution Amendment Bill is correct?
o: It can be introduced in a State legislature.
A deadlock is resolved by a joint sitting under Article 108.
It can be introduced by a private member without the President's prior permission.
State ratification requires a special majority in the State legislatures.
q.x: A private member can move it; there is no joint sitting; States ratify by simple majority; it starts only in Parliament.

q.s: Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment?
q.x: The 42nd Amendment added Socialist, Secular and Integrity.

q.s: 'Armed rebellion' replaced 'internal disturbance' as a ground for National Emergency by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) made this change.

q.s: In financial matters, which of the following can the Rajya Sabha NOT do?
o: Recommend changes to a Money Bill
Vote on the Demands for Grants
q.x: Only the Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants (Article 113).

q.s: The Vice-President of India is the ex officio President of the:
o: Indian Council of Social Science Research
q.x: The VP is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and President of the ICWA.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Vice-President of India is correct?
o: He is not a part of Parliament.
He is elected directly by the people.
He succeeds to the Presidency for the rest of the term on the President's death.
He is a member of the Rajya Sabha.
q.x: Parliament is the President and two Houses; on a vacancy the VP only acts until a new President is elected.

q.s: A non-member appointed Minister must become a Member of Parliament within:
q.x: Article 75(5): six consecutive months; S.R. Chaudhuri (2001) barred repeated re-appointment.

q.s: Under which Article can Parliament abolish a State Legislative Council on a resolution of the State Assembly?
q.x: Article 169: Parliament abolishes or creates a Council after the Assembly's special-majority resolution.

q.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 empowering Parliament to legislate on a State subject must be supported by:
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
q.x: It needs two-thirds of members present and voting and remains in force for one year, renewable.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: An Article 249 resolution needs two-thirds of the total membership of the Rajya Sabha.
An Article 249 resolution remains in force for six months only.
The Rajya Sabha can move a censure motion against the Council of Ministers.
An Article 249 resolution remains in force for one year and can be renewed.
q.x: It needs two-thirds of members present and voting and lasts one year; censure motions are moved only in the Lok Sabha.

q.s: After Uttar Pradesh, which State has the largest number of seats in both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?
q.x: Maharashtra has 48 Lok Sabha and 19 Rajya Sabha seats, second to UP (80/31).

q.s: Telangana's representation in Parliament is:
o: 28 Lok Sabha and 12 Rajya Sabha seats
14 Lok Sabha and 6 Rajya Sabha seats
25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats
17 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha seats
q.x: Telangana has 17 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha seats.

q.s: In Parliament, starred questions are printed on paper of which colour?
q.x: Starred – green; unstarred – white; short notice – light pink; to a private member – yellow.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (type of question – colour of paper) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Question to a private member – Yellow
q.x: Unstarred questions are printed on white paper.

q.s: The calling attention motion, an Indian parliamentary innovation, was introduced in:
q.x: Calling attention dates from 1954, the short-duration discussion from 1953; Zero Hour is not in the Constitution.

q.s: Which of the following parliamentary devices is NOT mentioned in the Constitution or the Rules of Procedure?
q.x: Zero Hour is an informal Indian innovation, not in the Constitution or Rules.

q.s: The Railway Budget was separated from the General Budget in 1924 on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Acworth Committee led to separation in 1924; the budgets were merged in 2017.

q.s: The first combined Railway and General Budget was presented on 1 February 2017 by:
q.x: Arun Jaitley presented the first merged budget.

q.s: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921 under the:
q.x: The PAC was set up in 1921 under the 1919 Act; an Opposition chairman since 1967 is a convention.

q.s: The Public Accounts Committee mainly examines the audit reports of the:
q.x: The PAC examines the Appropriation and Finance Accounts and CAG reports.

q.s: Compared with the UK, a key concern about the Indian Parliament is that:
o: Every Bill is examined by joint committees
Less than one-fifth of Bills are referred to committees
q.x: In India fewer than a fifth of Bills go to committees, whereas every UK Bill is examined by committees of both Houses.

q.s: Which of the following can the President NOT do with a Money Bill passed by Parliament?
o: Assent on the advice of the Cabinet
q.x: A Money Bill cannot be returned; the President may only assent or withhold assent.

q.s: Under Article 85, the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is:
q.x: Article 85 caps the interval at six months.

q.s: An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within ______ of its reassembly.
q.x: An ordinance lapses six weeks after reassembly unless disapproved earlier.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Governor's functions under Articles 174 and 176 are exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers?
q.x: Nabam Rebia (2016) – so the Governor's address must reflect Cabinet policy.

q.s: Who among the following law officers has the right to take part in the proceedings of Parliament under Article 88?
q.x: Only the Attorney General has the Article 88 right; the Solicitor General is the second law officer.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Solicitor General can take part in Parliament's proceedings under Article 88.
The Solicitor General is the second law officer of India, after the Attorney General.
The Solicitor General is appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
The Solicitor General is appointed on the advice of the UPSC.
q.x: The SG is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet and has no Article 88 right.

q.s: The Supreme Court's power to pass any order for doing 'complete justice' is provided under:
q.x: Article 142; e.g., the highway liquor ban in K. Balu (2016).

q.s: A legislature can lawfully overcome a court judgment by:
o: Asking the President to set it aside
Enacting a validating law removing the basis of the judgment
Referring it to the Election Commission
q.x: A validating law that removes the judgment's basis is permissible; a mere resolution cannot overrule a judgment.

q.s: The Supreme Court's power to do 'complete justice', often criticised in the judicial overreach debate, is under:
q.x: Critics note 'complete justice' in Art 142 is undefined and may bypass democratic scrutiny.

q.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the:
q.x: NGT appeals lie to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

q.s: Which of the following Acts is NOT included in Schedule I of the NGT Act, 2010?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
q.x: The Wild Life Act is not among the seven Acts of Schedule I.

q.s: Article 371D of the Constitution contains special provisions for:
q.x: 371D – Andhra Pradesh; 371A – Nagaland; 371J – Karnataka (Hyderabad-Karnataka region).

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Article 371J concerns the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka.

q.s: Article 268A, dealing with service tax, was omitted by the:
q.x: The 101st (GST) Amendment omitted Article 268A.

q.s: Which of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of taxes under Article 270?
q.x: Surcharges and cesses are outside the divisible pool.

q.s: Under the 2023 Act, the Selection Committee for the Chief Election Commissioner consists of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and:
o: A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM
q.x: The CJI was replaced by a Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM; the Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The 2023 Act retained the 1991 Act on the CEC and ECs.
The Search Committee is headed by the Prime Minister.
The Selection Committee may consider persons not shortlisted by the Search Committee.
The Selection Committee includes the Chief Justice of India.
q.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister; the CJI was replaced by a Cabinet Minister; the 2023 Act replaced the 1991 Act.

q.s: Under Article 321, the functions of the UPSC may be extended to local and corporate bodies by:
o: An executive order of the Home Ministry
q.x: An Act of Parliament (or State Legislature for an SPSC) can extend the functions.

q.s: India's first Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926 on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Lee Commission (1924) recommended it; Sir Ross Barker was the first chairman.

q.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for:
o: A Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs
q.x: The 1935 Act provided for a Federal PSC and provincial PSCs; the Federal PSC became the UPSC in 1950.

q.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status under:
q.x: The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Art 338B; Art 338A is the NCST (89th Amendment).

q.s: The separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was created by the:
q.x: The 89th Amendment (2003) split the combined commission; NCST came into being in 2004.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides safeguards to civil servants against arbitrary dismissal?
q.x: Art 311 – safeguards; 309 – recruitment and service conditions; 317 – removal of PSC members; 320 – PSC functions.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – subject) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 320 – Functions of Public Service Commissions
Article 309 – Recruitment and conditions of service
Article 317 – Functions of Public Service Commissions
q.x: Article 317 deals with removal and suspension of PSC members.

q.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission was constituted in:
q.x: The Second ARC (chair Veerappa Moily) came in 2005; the First ARC in 1966.

q.s: The first report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealt with:
q.x: Its first report was on RTI; Ethics in Governance was the fourth.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
q.x: Sukumar Sen; V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman CEC.

q.s: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the:
q.x: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age to 18.

q.s: After the 2019 amendment to the RTI Act, the term of Information Commissioners is:
o: Five years or 65 years of age
Four years or 65 years of age
Three years, as prescribed by the Centre
q.x: Since 2019 the Centre prescribes term and salary; the rules fix three years.

q.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended that the Inter-State Council should meet at least:
q.x: ISC thrice a year; Zonal Councils twice; NIC once a year.

q.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations was set up in:
q.x: Sarkaria was set up in 1983 and reported in 1988; Punchhi in 2007.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee on Centre-State relations was appointed by the government of:
q.x: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by the Tamil Nadu government.

q.s: The Nationalist Congress Party was founded in 1999 by Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma and:
q.x: The three were removed from the Congress over Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin.

q.s: The DMK formed its first government in Tamil Nadu in 1967 under:
q.x: Annadurai led the DMK to power in 1967.

q.s: The Asom Gana Parishad was launched in 1985 under the leadership of:
q.x: The AGP was launched at Golaghat on 14 October 1985 under Prafulla Kumar Mahanta.

q.s: Political parties are registered by the Election Commission under Section 29A of the:
q.x: Registration is under s.29A of the RPA, 1951; recognition under the Symbols Order, 1968.

q.s: EVMs in India are manufactured by BEL and:
q.x: BEL (Bengaluru) and ECIL (Hyderabad) make EVMs.

q.s: An M3 EVM control unit can be linked to a maximum of how many ballot units?
q.x: An M3 takes 24 ballot units (384 candidates incl. NOTA); an M2 only 4.

q.s: Which Law Commission report recommended disqualifying candidates once charges are framed in serious offences?
q.x: The 244th (2014) dealt with disqualification; the 255th (2015) with electoral reforms like the totaliser.

q.s: The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill (1989) on Panchayati Raj was defeated in the:
q.x: It passed the Lok Sabha but was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989.

q.s: The 64th Amendment Bill to give constitutional status to Panchayats was introduced by the government of:
q.x: The Rajiv Gandhi government introduced it in July 1989.

q.s: Panchayats can levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees under:
o: Article 243H, as authorised by the State Legislature
q.x: Panchayats have no independent taxing power; Article 243H lets the State Legislature authorise them.

q.s: Which committee is associated with tax reforms in 1991?
q.x: Chelliah – tax reforms; Narasimham – banking; Malhotra – insurance; Rangarajan – disinvestment.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (committee – subject) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Rangarajan Committee (1993) dealt with disinvestment of PSUs.

q.s: Under the disinvestment method 'Institutional Placement Programme', shares are offered to:
q.x: IPP is for QIBs; strategic sale transfers shares plus management control.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a method of disinvestment of PSUs?
q.x: Open market operations are an RBI monetary tool.

q.s: Good Governance Day, observed on 25 December, marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: It marks Vajpayee's birthday and was first observed in 2014.

q.s: In the Good Governance Index 2021, which State ranked first overall?
q.x: Gujarat ranked first overall; AP ranked first in agriculture and allied sectors.

q.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, Indian Railways was to examine establishing a new railway zone in:
q.x: AP's railway item was a new zone (South Coast Railway, Visakhapatnam); a Rail Coach Factory was Telangana's item.

q.s: As per NFHS-5 (2019-21), India's Total Fertility Rate is:
q.x: India's TFR is 2.0, below replacement level (2.1); Bihar is highest at 3.0; AP's is 1.7.

q.s: As per NFHS-5, which State has the highest Total Fertility Rate?
q.x: Bihar has the highest TFR (3.0).

q.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana (2005), launched under the National Rural Health Mission, aims to promote:
q.x: JSY gives cash assistance for institutional delivery; it replaced the National Maternity Benefit Scheme.

q.s: The Smart Cities Mission has been extended up to:
q.x: The mission was extended to 2025-26; the Centre gives about Rs 100 crore per city per year.

q.s: The Family Doctor Programme of Andhra Pradesh was launched on:
q.x: It began on 6 April 2023; PHC doctors visit village health clinics every 15 days.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the five new medical colleges opened in Andhra Pradesh in September 2023?
q.x: The five were Vizianagaram, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Rajamahendravaram and Nandyal.

q.s: As per SRS 2021-23, Andhra Pradesh's Maternal Mortality Ratio is:
q.x: AP's MMR is 30 against 88 for India; AP's IMR is 19 against 25 nationally.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Female life expectancy in Andhra Pradesh (73.3) is above the national figure.
Andhra Pradesh's IMR is higher than India's.
q.x: India's MMR is 88; AP's IMR (19) is below India's (25); AP's TFR is 1.5.

q.s: According to NFHS-6, stunting among children under 5 fell from 35.5% (NFHS-5) to:
q.x: Stunting fell to 29.3%, while underweight barely moved (32.1% to 31.8%).

q.s: The GDP deflator is calculated as:
q.x: Deflator = nominal ÷ real × 100; it covers all goods and services in GDP, unlike WPI/CPI baskets.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: A rising GDP deflator indicates rising purchasing power of money.
A rising GDP deflator indicates falling purchasing power of money.
The GDP deflator covers only a fixed basket of goods and services.
GDP deflator = real GDP ÷ nominal GDP × 100.
q.x: A rising deflator means prices are rising; deflator = nominal ÷ real × 100, covering all goods and services in GDP.

q.s: In the PLFS, the Unemployment Rate is defined as unemployed persons as a percentage of the:
q.x: UR = unemployed ÷ labour force × 100; unemployed ÷ population is the Proportion Unemployed.

q.s: The Labour Force Participation Rate includes:
o: Only those in the organised sector
q.x: The labour force is the employed plus those seeking work.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four institutional sectors for which GVA is compiled in India?
q.x: The four are general government, public corporations, private corporations and households.

q.s: The N.C. Saxena Committee (2009) of the Ministry of Rural Development dealt with:
o: Method for the rural BPL Census
q.x: Saxena – rural BPL Census; Hashim – urban BPL; Abhijit Sen – SECC indicators; Tendulkar – poverty estimation.

q.s: The National Development Council was set up in 1952 by:
q.x: The NDC was neither constitutional nor statutory.

q.s: Which commission recommended renaming the NDC as the National Economic and Development Council?
q.x: Sarkaria also suggested constitutional status under Article 263.

q.s: Which body gave final approval to the Five Year Plans before they went to the Union Cabinet and Parliament?
q.x: The NDC approved the draft prepared by the Planning Commission and was thus the apex body.

q.s: Which committee (1957) recommended that planning be entrusted to Panchayati Raj institutions?
q.x: Balwantrai Mehta (1957) recommended democratic decentralisation; Thungon made the Zila Parishad the pivot.

q.s: The 'Plan Holiday' with three Annual Plans was during:
q.x: Plan Holiday 1966-69; Rolling Plan 1978-80; Annual Plans 1990-92.

q.s: The 'Rolling Plan' was introduced by the:
q.x: The Janata Government introduced the Rolling Plan (1978-80).

q.s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, the threshold for prior government permission for lay-off was raised from 100 to:
q.x: It was raised to 300 workers.

q.s: Under the Code on Social Security, maternity leave is:
q.x: The Code provides 26 weeks of maternity leave and covers gig and platform workers.

q.s: Clauses (bb) and (c) of Article 280(3), on the Finance Commission's role for local bodies, were added by the:
q.x: They were added in 1992 to augment the State's Consolidated Fund on the State Finance Commission's advice.

q.s: Measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for local bodies are suggested by the Finance Commission on the basis of recommendations of the:
q.x: It relies on the State Finance Commission's recommendations.

q.s: A criticism of the 16th Finance Commission's GDP criterion in horizontal devolution is that it:
q.x: Critics say the GDP criterion rewards the size of an economy rather than need.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Fiscal capacity is uniform across States, so devolution equalises them by itself.
The 16th Finance Commission marks a shift from performance-based to entitlement-based transfers.
The 16th Finance Commission marks a shift from entitlement-based to performance-based transfers.
The GDP criterion of the 16th FC is praised for rewarding need rather than size.
q.x: The shift is towards performance; critics say fiscal capacity is not uniform and the GDP criterion rewards size.

q.s: The Gadgil formula for the distribution of central plan assistance was first used from the:

Andhra Pradesh computes constant-price GSDP at 2004-05 prices.

q.s: As per the Budget estimates, Andhra Pradesh's outstanding debt for 2026-27 is about:
q.x: 2026-27 BE is ₹7,11,094 crore, about 36% of GSDP.

After paddy, which is now Andhra Pradesh's second most important cereal?

q.s: In undivided Andhra Pradesh, which district had the largest area under food crops?

o: High Altitude and Tribal zone – Chintapalle

q.s: Compared with 2001-02, the number of cooperative societies in Andhra Pradesh has:

q.s: The 'Neeru-Chettu' programme of Andhra Pradesh, launched on 2 October 2014, aimed at:

q.s: The ratio of gross irrigated area to gross cropped area in Andhra Pradesh (about 52%) is:
q.x: AP's 52% is below India's 55.8%.

o: Andhra Pradesh's gross irrigated area in 2024-25 was smaller than its net irrigated area.
Andhra Pradesh's GIA/GCA ratio is higher than the national ratio.
Gross irrigated area can never be less than net irrigated area.
Net irrigated area counts land irrigated more than once.

q.s: The Hirakud dam on the Mahanadi is in:

q.s: Which of the following multipurpose projects is NOT correctly matched with its State?
o: Bhakra Nangal – Himachal Pradesh and Punjab
q.x: The Damodar Valley project is in Jharkhand and West Bengal.

q.s: The National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre at Chintaladevi (Nellore) was set up under the:
q.x: National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres come under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.

q.s: Under AP's IDP 4.0, an 'Ultra-Mega' project is one with investment of:
q.x: Ultra-Mega is above Rs 5,000 crore; Mega Rs 1,001-5,000 crore.

q.x: Orvakal – HBIC; Krishnapatnam – CBIC; Kopparthy – VCIC.

q.s: The PRASHAD scheme for pilgrimage rejuvenation is run by the Union Ministry of:
q.x: PRASHAD belongs to the Ministry of Tourism.

q.x: The Tropic of Capricorn, not Cancer, crosses Australia.

q.s: An instrument that only shows that an earthquake occurred and its time, without recording it, is a:

q.x: At Devprayag the Bhagirathi joins and the river becomes the Ganga.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Pindar joins the Alaknanda at Karnaprayag.

q.s: The Gandikota canyon, called the 'Grand Canyon of India', was carved by the river:
q.x: The Penna (Pennar) carved the Gandikota gorge in Kadapa district.

q.x: The Tsangpo enters Arunachal Pradesh through the Dihang gorge.

q.x: Groynes are hard structures built across the longshore drift to trap sand.

q.x: The Dardanelles links the Marmara with the Aegean; the Bosphorus links the Black Sea with the Marmara.

q.x: The Bering Strait separates Asia and North America, linking the Pacific and Arctic.

q.s: A rainbow is seen when:
o: The Sun is in front of the observer
There are no clouds in the sky
The Sun is behind the observer and raindrops are in front
q.x: A rainbow is seen with the Sun behind and drops in front; in a primary rainbow red is on the outside.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: In a primary rainbow, red appears on the outer side.
A corona is formed by refraction through ice crystals.
A secondary rainbow is formed by one internal reflection.
In a primary rainbow, red appears on the inner side.

q.x: Lysimeter – evapotranspiration; hydrometer – density; sling psychrometer – humidity.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (instrument – measures) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: A hydrometer measures the density of a liquid.

q.s: A hot, dry, stable air mass that forms over the Sahara and Arabia is classified as:
q.x: Continental tropical (cT); mT forms over warm oceans.

q.x: Maritime polar (mP); cA is the very cold dry Arctic air mass.

q.x: Green – no warning; yellow – be aware; orange – be prepared; red – take action.

q.x: El Nino brings drought to Indonesia and northern Australia, and often weak monsoons to India.

o: The El Nino of 2002 brought no drought to India.
About 6 of 10 El Nino years brought depressed rainfall to India.
Every El Nino year has caused a drought in India.
El Nino increases post-monsoon cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.

The Earth is closest to the Sun
The Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth
The Sun, Moon and Earth are in a straight line

q.x: Improper disposal of radioactive waste is also a nuclear hazard.

o: Assessment of the adequacy of safety measures
q.x: HAZOP (Hazard and Operability) studies assess the adequacy of safety measures.

q.x: Mitigation is the most cost-effective; EOCs belong to preparedness, compensation to recovery.
